subtitle: Using a phone's serial number as its unique identifier in SIP

tldr.problem: Mobile devices (GSM, UMTS, LTE) need a globally unique identifier when registering with IP Multimedia Subsystem (IMS) services. The IMEI (phone serial number) is the only identifier that works across both circuit-switched and IP domains.
tldr.mechanism: This RFC specifies how the GSMA IMEI Uniform Resource Name (URN) can be used as the instance-id in the '+sip.instance' Contact header field parameter, allowing devices to be uniquely identified in SIP registrations.
tldr.outcome: Mobile networks can now consistently identify devices through SIP, enabling emergency calls with device identification, preventing stolen device registration, and supporting handover between IP and circuit-switched domains.

today: RFC 7255 is an Informational RFC that specifies how the GSMA IMEI URN is used in SIP instance-ids for 3GPP IMS networks. It has not been obsoleted and remains the current specification for IMEI-based SIP registration.

sections.title: Identifying Phones in SIP Networks
sections.content:
The Session Initiation Protocol (SIP) uses the '+sip.instance' Contact header field parameter to contain a Uniform Resource Name (URN) that uniquely identifies a specific User Agent (UA) instance—a particular phone or device. SIP registrars use this instance-id to recognize that contacts from multiple registrations correspond to the same device.

RFC 5626 requires that a UA should create a UUID URN as its instance-id but allows other URN schemes. This RFC specifies how the GSMA IMEI URN—a URN built from a phone's International Mobile station Equipment Identity (IMEI), its globally unique serial number—can be used as the instance-id. RFC 7254 specifies how to construct the GSMA IMEI URN; this document specifies how to use it in '+sip.instance'.

The IMEI is a globally unique identifier for GSM, UMTS, and LTE mobile devices, allocated and managed by the GSMA. Every such device manufactured has an allocated IMEI. This specification enables 3GPP (Third Generation Partnership Project) networks to use the IMEI as the instance-id, meeting requirements for device identification in emergency calls, theft prevention, and seamless session handover between IP/IMS mode and circuit-switched mode.
sections.eli5: When a phone signs into a system, it needs to prove it is the same phone that signed in before. The phone's serial number (IMEI) is the perfect way to prove that.

sections.title: Why the IMEI Matters for Mobile Calls
sections.content:
Mobile networks have evolved from pure circuit-switched systems (GSM) to mixed IP and circuit-switched systems. Today's LTE networks use IP for all services, but the global transition to all-IP, SIP-based IMS networks will take many years. This means mobile devices must operate in both IP/SIP/IMS mode and circuit-switched mode simultaneously.

For voice calls and sessions, devices may be handed over between IP/SIP/IMS mode and circuit-switched mode mid-call. Some sessions may have media delivered via both domains to the same device. To achieve this, the mobile device must be simultaneously attached via both IP/SIP/IMS and circuit-switched domains.

To maintain session continuity between domains, 3GPP has specified the Mobile Switching Center (MSC) server enhanced for IMS Centralized Services (ICS) and enhanced for Single Radio Voice Call Continuity (SR-VCC). These servers perform SIP registration on behalf of the mobile device while the device also directly registers with SIP/IMS. The only mobile device identifier that is transportable using GSM/UMTS/LTE signaling is the IMEI.

Regulatory requirements may require that the IMEI be provided to the Public Safety Answering Point (PSAP) for emergency calls, and the IMEI can be used to prevent stolen devices from accessing the network and to identify devices in unauthenticated emergency sessions.
sections.eli5: Old phones were pure circuit-switched. New phones handle both circuit and data. When a call hands over between them, the IMEI is the only number that both systems understand.

sections.title: How Devices and Registrars Use IMEI
sections.content:
User Agent Client (UAC) procedures: A UAC (phone) that has an IMEI and is registering with a 3GPP IMS network MUST include the GSMA IMEI URN in the '+sip.instance' media feature tag according to RFC 7254 syntax when performing registrations per RFC 5626 and RFC 5627 or any procedure requiring '+sip.instance'. The UAC should not include the optional 'svn' (software version) parameter, since firmware upgrades can change this and create new instance-ids. Future non-zero values of the 'vers' parameter will require an update to this RFC.

The UAC must provide character-by-character identical URNs in each registration—any optional or variable components must have the same values and order in every registration as in the first. A UAC must not use the GSMA IMEI URN as an instance-id except when registering with a 3GPP IMS network; when operating outside IMS mode, it should use a UUID as specified in RFC 5626. The '+sip.instance' tag containing IMEI must not be included in non-REGISTER requests except those related to emergency sessions.

3GPP SIP Registrar procedures: When a SIP registrar in 3GPP IMS receives a '+sip.instance' media feature tag containing the GSMA IMEI URN in the Contact header field, it follows the procedures of RFC 5626. The IMEI URN may be validated per RFC 7254. If the UA indicates support for RFC 5627 and the registrar allocates a public GRUU (Globally Routable User Agent URI), the instance-id must be obfuscated in the 'gr' parameter to avoid revealing the IMEI to other UAs.
sections.eli5: A phone includes its serial number in every sign-in, always using the exact same format. A server accepts it and keeps it secret in its forwarding addresses, so other phones do not see the device's serial number.

sections.title: Privacy and Security Requirements
sections.content:
IMEIs, like other instance-ids, can be correlated to a user and are personally identifiable information. They must be treated the same way as any other personally identifiable information: the '+sip.instance' media feature tag containing the GSMA IMEI URN must not be included in requests or responses intended to convey anonymity, as this could violate user privacy.

Publication of the GSMA IMEI URN to networks to which the UA is not attached, or with which it does not have a service relationship, is a security breach. Service provider network elements must not forward the '+sip.instance' media feature tag toward the destination UA when forwarding requests or responses. An instance-id containing the GSMA IMEI URN identifies a mobile device, not a user, and must not be used alone as an address for a user or as user identification credentials.

Entities that log the instance-id must protect them as personally identifiable information; regulatory requirements may require carriers to log SIP IMEIs. To protect the '+sip.instance' media feature tag from tampering, REGISTER requests containing the GSMA IMEI URN must be sent using a security mechanism such as Transport Layer Security (TLS) or another mechanism providing equivalent protection, such as hop-by-hop IPsec.
sections.eli5: A phone's serial number is private information, like a social security number. It should only be sent over secure connections, never shared with networks the phone is not registered with, and never used to prove who the user is.
